parameters.content:
## Send a weekly summary of open quotes to follow up with Gmail

For service businesses that keep their quotes in a Google Sheet and want one email a week instead of opening it every day.

### How it works
1. Every Monday at 8:00 the workflow groups the sheet rows by `status`.
2. You get one email: open quotes and their value, quotes won and lost since the last summary, the close rate, and the quotes open too long.
3. Closed quotes get a date in `closed_at`, so each one is counted once.

The first run counts every quote already closed in the sheet.

### Setup
1. Use the sheet described in the **Sheet** note.
2. Pick your Google Sheets credential and paste your sheet URL in **Document** in **Read all quotes** and **Mark as counted**. Pick your Gmail credential in **Send weekly summary**.
3. Edit **Settings**: change `owner_email` to your email first, then currency symbol and time zone. Set Workflow settings > Timezone to the same zone.
4. To see it now, click Execute workflow. A test run also marks closed quotes as counted, so they will not show in Monday's email.
5. Activate.

If nothing happens, open **Executions** to see the error.

### Requirements
- Google Sheets and Gmail credentials in n8n: docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/credentials/google/. If your Google Cloud app is External and in Testing, the connection expires after 7 days; publish it to avoid this.
- Statuses, in lowercase. Waiting: `missing_info`, `ready_to_quote`. Open: `quote_sent`, `review`, `replied`. Won: `accepted`, `booking_sent`, `scheduled`. Lost: `lost`, `no_reply`.
- By hand: set `quote_sent`, and fill `quote_amount` (numbers only, dot for cents: 1200.50) and `quote_sent_at` (like 2026-10-14; if Sheets changes it, format the column as Plain text).
- `old_after_days` in **Settings**: when an open quote counts as old.

One person is behind Small Hours. AI agents built and tested this template.

### Sheet: tab named `Requests`
Same sheet as the quote request template. To create it, paste this line in cell A1, then Data > Split text to columns:
`request_id,received_at,status,name,email,phone,service,address,preferred_date,details,missing_fields,quote_id,quote_amount,thread_id,quote_sent_at,follow_ups_sent,last_follow_up_at,reply_label,job_start,event_id,closed_at`

## 1. Set your details
Your email first, then currency, time zone and when a quote counts as old.

## 2. Every Monday it counts your quotes
Reads every row and builds the email. Open quotes are counted by age, closed ones only if `closed_at` is empty.
